text_en: Moldova is between having some and a moderate level of preparation in the area of freedom of movement for workers.

Good progress was made during the reporting period by signing further social security coordination agreements with EU Member States (Slovakia) and continuing work to prepare for joining the European Network of Employment Services (EURES) upon accession, notably by establishing the national legal framework for EURES activities and designating the National Employment Agency (NEA) as the National Coordination Office (NCO).

Some progress was made during the reporting period, including the launch of the new State Register of Legal Entities, a strengthened Public Audit Oversight Council, and adoption of amendments to the Corporate Governance Code.
Moldova is moderately prepared in the area of digital transformation and media.
Good progress was made, as the government continued to implement the Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030 and advanced on its key performance indicators.
Good progress was made in further aligning national legislation with the EU acquis in the areas of indirect and direct taxation, excise duties, and the digitalisation of tax administration services.

The country has made good progress, notably through the implementation of the New Computerised Transit System (NCTS) and formal accession to the Common Transit Convention (CTC) and the Convention on the Simplification of Formalities in Trade in Goods.
There was some progress on 5G deployment with population coverage estimated at 25- 35%
On semiconductors, Moldova has made some progress by adopting the Law on the protection of topographies of semiconductor products in April 2026 but is yet to align with the Chips Act.
